key: All that is bare he covers o’er, all that is sick he medicines; The blind man sees, the cripple walks.
s: Early in a hymn to Soma, before prayers against enmity, the verse lists what he mends; Sāyaṇa, on 8.68.2, reads the covering as fruit for what lies fruitless, or as cloth he brings forth, and the healing as given through the sacrifice and as medicine.

evidence.gloss: This Soma covers whatever is naked. Whatever stands as if naked, fruitless, he covers with fruit; or else, bringing forth cloth, he covers it. Likewise whatever is sick, all of that he heals: through the sacrifice, as the means to heaven, and in the form of medicine, as the means to the body’s well-being.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 8.68.2 at [687,2]; standard 8.79.2); deity Soma per the Anukramaṇī in Sāyaṇa’s introduction and Wilson. Sāyaṇa on 8.79.2 glosses the covering first as covering what is naked, then as covering the fruitless with fruit, OR as covering by producing cloth; the healing through sacrifice (for heaven) and as medicine (for the body). Corrected: the proposal gave only the fruit gloss as his reading and drifted to barren/clothing; the sentence now carries both of his alternatives, and the context clause was shortened to keep 44 words. Source line and place kept (revision 202004 dated 2019-05-18 by the Wikisource API).
